title: Zhang et al. (2021) section 4.3 parameters: uniform 2D Drucker-Prager validation

governing_assumptions: pressure-independent associated Drucker-Prager with Inscribed mapping and zero friction/dilation
same pure-shear peak/residual strength as the paper Tresca model; the general stress-space yield surfaces differ

geometry.description: 5 m high plateau to x=20 m and 45 degree slope to x=25 m

discretization.refinement_plan: Original coarse uniform 0.2 m grid only. AdaptiveGrid is not configured in validation.

materials.name: sensitive clay
materials.provenance: Paper section 4.3: cp/cr=20/4 kPa, H=-50 kPa => standard accumulated DP equivalent strain endpoint 0.32. At zero friction Inscribed DP has sqrt(J2)=c, preserving the prescribed pure-shear strength.

initial_conditions.stress_or_pressure: Elastic dynamic relaxation with identical E, nu, density and boundaries, before enabling plasticity; relaxed geometry and stress transferred on device; velocity reset to zero. Relaxation uses alphaPIC=1 and local damping 0.7; maximum particle speed <0.002 m/s within 10 s.

boundary_conditions.provenance: Section 4.3 pp.11-12, main case mu=0.3; secondary case mu=0.1

time.stability_policy: Conservative fixed MPM dt checked by native CFL at finest grid; paper uses adaptive SPFEM CFL factor 0.9, not transferred as an MPM timestep.

validation.observable: Maximum relative mass drift on the uniform grid

invariants.basis: Float64 particle mass on a uniform grid without particle splitting.

paper_comparison.source: Zhang et al., Computers and Geotechnics 129 (2021) 103856, section 4.3, Figs.15-18
paper_comparison.measurement: Runout = current rightmost particle edge minus original toe x=25 m. Retrogression = original crest x=20 m minus current head-scarp top; report threshold sensitivity.
paper_comparison.acceptance: Report relative deviations; no preset claim of agreement for mesh-dependent local softening with different spatial methods.

assumptions: Paper 3D width is omitted; x-z section maps to computational x-y, strict plane strain and unit thickness.
Gravity magnitude is not stated in section 4.3; use standard g=9.81 m/s^2.

Paper does not give a 2D mesh spacing, relaxation damping/tolerance or plastic potential. Use documented MPM discretization and the zero-angle DP associated shear potential; do not tune physical parameters to match the result.
Paper has no regularisation; local strain softening remains mesh dependent.
Original basal nodes fixed as in Fig.15; Coulomb ground contact outside the original toe.
DP epdstrain accumulates the standard equivalent plastic-strain increment; for zero dilation its endpoint is 0.32, with no MC sqrt(2) conversion.
The paper uses Tresca; this requested DP comparison preserves the pure-shear strength and softening slope, not the entire Tresca surface.
Native DP history includes the full plastic-flow norm, including volumetric tensile-cap flow; equality with the paper deviatoric invariant holds for zero-dilation shear, not every loading branch.
